issue.title: Album schema-writer e2e self-test: held-lock apply makes 2 commits instead of 1
issue.description:
`scripts/obsidian-album-schema-writer-e2e.cjs --self-test` fails its held-lock scenario:
`Error: held-lock apply must create exactly one commit, saw 2` (selfTest, script line ~643).

The scenario holds the vault lock with a holder process, previews a `choice.add` on the
`eat` album through `createAlbumUpdateSession`, applies through real
`bob albums update eat -f json -i -`, and expects exactly one new commit after the wait.
Two commits appear.

Evidence:
- bob-cli-ms.4 note #3: reproduced on clean bob-plugins 137c77f with that phase stashed.
- bob-cli-ms.5 note #2: still failing with BOB_BIN=/home/bryan/.cargo/bin/bob (bob 0.5.0).
- bob-cli-ms.land (2026-11-18): reproduced again on bob-plugins origin/master f8a8619 with
  BOB_BIN=/home/bryan/.cargo/bin/bob (bob 0.5.0, built from bob-cli master with the
  records envelope). Command: `BOB_BIN=$HOME/.cargo/bin/bob node
  scripts/obsidian-album-schema-writer-e2e.cjs --self-test` → exit 1.

The Record Card epic (bob-cli-ms) never touches `bob albums update` or the album session;
its own record-writer self-test passes. Root cause unknown: find out where the second
commit comes from (the holder process, a pre/post vault-sync commit, or a bob-cli
change in lock/commit behavior since the self-test was written), then fix the writer or
the test's expectation, whichever is wrong.
